question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{12}{\sqrt[3]{{s}^{7}}}\,\text{d}s & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{12}{\sqrt[3]{{s}^{7}}}\,\text{d}s \\  & =12{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}{s}^{-7/3}\,\text{d}s \\  & =12{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-\frac{3}{4}{s}^{-4/3}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{s}^{4}}}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{a}^{4}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{1}^{4}}}) \\  & =-9(0-1) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
